world: B/S UNSEPARATED -- displacement and selection both predict this, and this design cannot tell them apart
outcome_variable_scope: Released human weights only. No judge, no model, no ranking enters this round.
scope: Provenance is r48's identification by rating count -- criteria rated by at least 6 raters are the pre-seeded set shown to everyone, singly-rated ones are participant write-ins. The permutation is WITHIN prompt, so a prompt whose criteria are all rated softly cannot create a provenance effect. This measures scale USE, not what a neutral option would have produced -- that arm does not exist in this release and is preregistered.
verdict: B/S UNSEPARATED -- displacement and selection both predict this, and this design cannot tell them apart. THE MIDPOINT OF A 21-POINT SCALE WAS USED ONCE IN 102,147 RATINGS (0.000010), and no round in this package had read that distribution out. Queue item 1 rescoped 'not a forced-choice artifact' to 'robust to POST-HOC criterion abstention' precisely because r35 could not simulate an elicitation-time neutral option; this round cannot simulate one either, and does not try. What it asks instead is whether the scale is used DIFFERENTLY where the pressure should differ -- a rater has an opinion about a criterion they wrote and may have none about one they were shown. Low-magnitude ratings (|w| in (1, 2)) are 0.1921 of seed ratings against 0.0698 of write-in ratings, a difference of +0.1223 against a within-prompt provenance-permutation null of [-0.0016,+0.0095]. SCALE-USE FACTS WORTH HAVING SEPARATELY FROM THE CONTRAST: 0.7701 of ratings are positive, 0.1696 sit at the extreme |w|=10, and 0.2955 fall on 5 or 10 -- so more than a third of all weight mass lands on two of the twenty-one available values, which is coarse mental rounding and bears on how much resolution any weighted aggregation can actually carry. ⚠ THE RIVAL I DID NOT WRITE BEFORE THE RUN, and it predicts the same direction: SELECTION. A rater authors a write-in because they already care about it, so it gets a strong weight; a rater is HANDED a seed regardless of whether they care. That yields more low-magnitude mass on seeds with no forced-choice pressure involved at all. The permutation null does not touch it -- it scrambles which class a criterion is in, not why the class exists -- so displacement and selection are UNSEPARATED here and the world label says so instead of naming the one I predicted. WHAT THIS CANNOT DO, unchanged from before the run: nobody in this release was offered a neutral option, so what they WOULD have done is unobservable. A null here would say the pressure is uniform across provenance, not that there is no pressure. WHAT WOULD SEPARATE THEM: the preregistered neutral-option arm. If the missing midpoint is doing the work, offering 'no general direction' should absorb most of the seed low-magnitude mass and little of the write-in mass -- a directional prediction this round contributes to Experiment 1 and cannot itself test.
